headings: Whether it be stolen or no.
It will be (or is intended to be stolen.)

units.short_original_anchor: his Lord for him that hath lost the Goods
units.normalized_historical_statement: The opening continuation assigns 'his Lord' to the person who has lost the goods and to the place from which the goods were taken. The antecedent of 'his' lies before this window.
preconditions: Continuation of a significator assignment begun on the preceding page.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The preceding words are unavailable in this window; the antecedent must not be supplied from memory.

units.short_original_anchor: the seventh house and his Lord, and the peregrine Planet
units.normalized_historical_statement: The seventh house and its lord, a peregrine planet in an angle, and the lord of the hour signify the thief or party who took away the goods.
preconditions: The peregrine planet specified here is in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No priority among these thief significators is stated in the visible continuation.

units.short_original_anchor: This is a very good judgment, and may well be trusted
units.normalized_historical_statement: A printed marginal note endorses the adjacent judgment as very good and trustworthy.
preconditions: The note accompanies the opening passage on printed page 332.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Its precise scope within the surrounding rules is not expressly delimited.

units.short_original_anchor: shall signifie the Goods or thing that is lost
units.normalized_historical_statement: The second house, its lord, and the Moon signify the goods or thing that is lost, stolen, or missing.
preconditions: A question concerns lost, stolen, or missing goods.

units.short_original_anchor: the fourth house and his Lord shall signifie the place
units.normalized_historical_statement: The fourth house and its lord signify the place where the goods were laid, put, done, or conveyed, and where they are at that instant.
preconditions: A question concerns the location of the goods.

units.short_original_anchor: shall tell and shew whether the Goods shall be found
units.normalized_historical_statement: The aspects of the Sun and Moon, the lord of the ascendant, the lord of the second, and the lord of the Moon's house to the lord of the ascendant, together with their applications and aspects to one another, indicate whether the goods will be found or recovered.
preconditions: Examine the named significators' aspects and applications.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sentence's punctuation does not clearly delimit every member of the aspect list.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods taken away by somebody
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the second and the Moon are in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh, and the lord of the seventh beholds them by trine or sextile, the goods have been taken away by somebody rather than simply lost.
preconditions: Lord of the second and Moon in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh.
Lord of the seventh beholds them by trine or sextile.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source permits the aspect to be 'long out', explaining this as many degrees distant.

units.short_original_anchor: it is neither lost nor stolen, but carelesly mislaid
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the second, occupies the house of the lord of the hour, and goes to conjunction with the lord of the seventh, the party left the goods somewhere they had been and forgot them; the goods are carelessly mislaid.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the second.
Moon is in the house of the lord of the hour.
Moon is going to conjunction with the lord of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: the thing is not stolen, but taken away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the ascendant and is in the fourth, while the lord of the second is in the seventh or in the sign of the eighth house, in conjunction to the second house and sextile or trine to the Moon, the thing was taken away in jest.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the ascendant and in the fourth.
Lord of the second is in the seventh or in the sign of the eighth house.
The printed text also requires conjunction 'to the second house'.
Sextile or trine to the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The unusual expression 'in conjunction to the second house' is retained without silently substituting another target.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods stolen and taken away
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the ascendant and is in the ascendant, not far remote, and the Sun rules the second and is in the third with the lord of the seventh, while the lord of the seventh oppresses the Moon by square, the goods are stolen and taken away.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the ascendant and in the ascendant, 'not farre remote'.
Sun is lord of the second and in the third with the lord of the seventh.
Lord of the seventh oppresses the Moon with a square.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The reference point of 'not farre remote' is not further explained.

units.short_original_anchor: Lord of the second also being Lord of the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the third and oppressed by the lord of the seventh through his square aspect, and the lord of the second also rules the ascendant and is in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Moon in the third.
Lord of the seventh oppresses the Moon by square.
Lord of the second also rules the ascendant.
That lord is in the seventh, in the sign of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: except the Sun and Moon behold the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: Within the preceding configuration, if the thing was taken in jest, recovery will be difficult unless the Sun and Moon behold the ascendant.
preconditions: The configuration of A2011.
The thing was taken in jest.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The Sun and Moon beholding the ascendant provide the stated exception to difficult recovery.
The anchor renders the printed solar and lunar glyphs as their names; the literal image has glyphs.

units.short_original_anchor: but overlooked and mistaken
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is 'the seventh' in the sign of the lord of the hour, and the lord of the hour rules the seventh, the goods are overlooked and mistaken rather than stolen or taken away.
preconditions: The Moon is described as 'the seventh' in the sign of the lord of the hour.
Lord of the hour is lord of the seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed opening appears to omit 'in' before 'the seventh'.
The short anchor is only four words because this diagnostic phrase is especially clear.

units.short_original_anchor: then hath the party lost the Goods as he went
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the fifth in Capricorn and rules the hour, Venus rules the second and is in the tenth in the sign of the seventh, and the Moon is in conjunction with the lord of the seventh, the party lost the goods while travelling or left them in a place they visited.
preconditions: Moon in the fifth and in Capricorn.
Moon is Lady of the hour.
Venus is Lady of the second, in the tenth, in the sign of the seventh.
Moon in conjunction with the lord of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: taken away in jest by the Master of the house
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the hour and is in Cancer in the eighth, the lord of the second is in the fifth, neither beholds the lord of the seventh, and the lord of the seventh is in the seventh, the master of the house took the goods in jest and will deny doing so.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the hour, in Cancer, in the eighth.
Lord of the second in the fifth.
Neither Moon nor lord of the second beholds the lord of the seventh.
Lord of the seventh in the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: then hath somebody taken the things away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the hour, is in the fourth, and is conjunct the lord of the seventh, while the lord of the second is in the twelfth and sextile the lord of the seventh, somebody took the things in jest.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the hour and in the fourth.
Moon conjunct the lord of the seventh.
Lord of the second in the twelfth.
Lord of the second sextile the lord of the seventh.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods taken away in jest
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon is in the sign of the lord of the seventh without beholding that lord, the Moon is in the twelfth, and the lord of the second is in the sixth, the goods were taken away in jest.
preconditions: Moon in the sign of the lord of the seventh.
Moon does not behold the lord of the seventh.
Moon in the twelfth.
Lord of the second in the sixth.

units.short_original_anchor: but will soone be had again
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the second last separated from the lord of the Moon's house, the goods were stolen in jest and will soon be recovered.
preconditions: Lord of the second last separated from the lord of the house occupied by the Moon.

units.short_original_anchor: the Goods is taken away and stolen by somebody
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon separates from the lord of the second by square, somebody has taken away and stolen the goods.
preconditions: Moon separates from the lord of the second by square.

units.short_original_anchor: separate from the lord of the house where in she is
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the Moon rules the second and separates from the lord of the house she occupies, the thing is stolen.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the second.
Moon separates from the lord of her occupied house.

units.short_original_anchor: then did the Querent lay it downe and forget it
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the ascendant separates from Jupiter or from the lord of the second house, the querent laid the thing down and forgot it, thereby losing it.
preconditions: Lord of the ascendant separates from Jupiter or from the lord of the second.

units.short_original_anchor: it is the surer
units.normalized_historical_statement: The foregoing judgment that the querent laid the thing down and forgot it is more certain when both the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the second separate from Jupiter.
preconditions: Both the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the second separate from Jupiter.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The diagnostic phrase contains only four words; its antecedent is A2021.

units.short_original_anchor: doth apply unto the lord of the second house
units.normalized_historical_statement: Another configuration supporting the foregoing judgment has the Moon ruling the ascendant, separating from Jupiter, and applying to the lord of the second, which also last separated from Jupiter.
preconditions: Moon is Lady of the ascendant.
Moon separates from Jupiter.
Moon applies to the lord of the second.
Lord of the second also last separated from Jupiter.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source says these configurations give one judgment, referring back to laying down and forgetting the goods.

units.short_original_anchor: yet if it be so, it giveth all one judgment
units.normalized_historical_statement: The same judgment applies when the lord of the ascendant, exemplified by the Sun, also rules the second and separates from Jupiter.
preconditions: One planet rules both ascendant and second.
That planet separates from Jupiter.
The source names the Sun in its parenthetical example.

units.short_original_anchor: then did the party lose the Goods by the way
units.normalized_historical_statement: If the lord of the second or Jupiter separates from the lord of the ascendant, the party lost the goods along their route, in a place they visited, or through their slipping privately from a pocket into a secret place; they are neither stolen nor found.
preconditions: Lord of the second or Jupiter separates from the lord of the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source lists alternative circumstances without selecting one.

units.short_original_anchor: then is the Goods absolutely stolen
units.normalized_historical_statement: If none of the foregoing separations exists, examine whether the peregrine planet, lord of the seventh, or Mercury acting for the thief applies to Jupiter or the lord of the second. If so, the goods are absolutely stolen and the thief came intending to steal.
preconditions: None of the separations previously described.
Peregrine planet, lord of the seventh, or Mercury as thief applies to Jupiter or the lord of the second.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sentence begins on PDF367 and continues on PDF368.
Mercury is expressly qualified here as a thief significator.

units.short_original_anchor: did offer it selfe to the Thiefe
units.normalized_historical_statement: Under the preceding absence of separations, if the lord of the second or Jupiter applies to the peregrine planet, lord of the seventh, or Mercury as thief, the goods offered themselves to the thief or were easily obtained. The taker came without an intention to steal, but saw the thing lying openly and carelessly, then took it away.
preconditions: Continuation of the examination introduced when the foregoing separations are absent.
Lord of the second or Jupiter applies to a named thief significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Application direction reverses A2026 and changes the attributed intention.

units.short_original_anchor: then the Querent did lose the thing by the way
units.normalized_historical_statement: The querent lost the thing while travelling, and it was not stolen, under the printed compound configuration: the Moon rules both ascendant and second, is in Taurus, and applies by conjunction to the Sun within one degree; the Sun rules the third; Mars is the peregrine planet and is in the tenth; Mercury applies to Mars; and none of the aforesaid separations or applications impedes. The passage additionally says 'or the lord of the seventh in the third' before its conclusion.
preconditions: Moon rules ascendant and second.
Moon in Taurus, applying by conjunction to the Sun within one degree.
Sun is lord of the third.
Mars is the peregrine planet and in the tenth.
Mercury applies to Mars.
No aforesaid separation or application impedes.
Printed additional alternative: lord of the seventh in the third.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The scope of the final 'or' is ambiguous; the source does not clearly establish whether it replaces the whole preceding configuration or only its immediately preceding clause.
